## What this does *not* do
- **It doesn't replace or duplicate compression your backend already does** (prompt caching, a compr
essing proxy). It forwards to your backend as-is once it has decided whether to compact first; the t

wo are complementary.
- **The count is exact only on llama.cpp and vLLM; everywhere else it is an es
timate, and an estimate is not always conservative.** On llama.cpp (`/apply-template`, then `/tokeni
ze`) and vLLM (`/tokenize` with the messages, `add_generation_prompt` and the tools) the upstream co
unts the request itself, chat template included, and that count decides compaction as it is: no cali
bration factor, no margin. Which of the two (if either) the upstream is comes only from the window d
etection that already runs, so **exact counts need context detection on (`GUARDIAN_DETECT_CONTEXT`,
on by default)**: no extra probe goes out on the request path, and with `GUARDIAN_DETECT_CONTEXT=0`
no tokenize or apply-template request is ever sent and counts are estimates. **On vLLM the exact cou
nt is asked only once the chat is big enough to matter**: while the estimate times 8 is still under
the input budget (the review's worst under-read is ×4) the estimate is used, so short chats cost the
tokenizer nothing; llama.cpp is counted on every request. On llama.cpp the next turn sends only the
new messages to be counted (plus one template-overhead probe per model), so a long conversation is

not re-tokenised each  [长行截断]
